title: Innovate
coreMove: Design a bounded innovation space where a new idea has enough autonomy to learn and enough accountability to stay honest.
sourcePressure: Established organizations need sandboxes, autonomy, protected resources, incentives, protection, and accountability so internal ventures can learn before the core business crushes them.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Assuming an innovation program needs only encouragement, budget, or executive slogans.

sourceAnchors.name: Innovation sandbox
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar names sandboxes as a structure that lets new ideas learn
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A sandbox is not a toy room; it is a boundary that keeps the core business from judging a question before it has evidence.

sourceAnchors.name: Protected resources
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says resources must be protected for entrepreneurial teams
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Protected resources buy time for learning, not immunity from proof.

hook: Do not open with a definition of Innovate.
Do not use a generic founder staring at a dashboard hook.
Do not start with broad claims about modern business.
counterintuition: Avoid the shell that speed is not the point, learning is the point.
Avoid a simple not X but Y correction if the same rhythm can be replaced by a concrete tension.
Avoid making caution sound like timidity.
tryThisNow: Do not ask the reader to set a timer and reflect.
Do not tell the reader to make a generic list of assumptions.
Do not use a reusable audit-your-work prompt without chapter terms.
examples: No six startup founders in meeting rooms.
No repeated coffee mug, marker, kitchen, classroom, or bus-stop shells.
No invented named case studies, famous companies, studies, or founders.
